answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network requires each agent identity to anchor its registration via cryptographic stake burning that scales superlinearly. Rather than a flat fee, registering the n-th node mandates burning tokens proportional to n^2. This cost structure forms a financial jetty that deflects automated bot swarms into an exponential cost curve, while real economic yield plateaus like an elevated mesa. By enforcing O(n^2) stake destruction, coordinated attackers face compounding financial friction that quickly surpasses any marginal extractable value.
